supply_chain.source: NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI)
supply_chain.raw_value: GSCPI +1.28 (Sep 2026) | WEI +3.33 (context, not scored) | BDRY $12.61 (context, not scored)
supply_chain.raw_label: Global Supply Chain Pressure (z-score; 0 = historical average)
supply_chain.description: The NY Fed's Global Supply Chain Pressure Index combines transport costs and supplier delivery times across major economies into one z-score, where 0 is the historical average. It stood at +1.28 for September 2026: supply chain pressure is well above its historical average. The score's normal (80) is the pre-2020 median. The index already includes the Baltic Dry Index, so the BDRY dry-bulk ETF and the Weekly Economic Index are shown for context and are not scored.
supply_chain.calculation: GSCPI is mapped through fixed anchors, lower being better: the healthiest 5% of pre-2020 months = 100, the pre-2020 median = 80, the worst month on record = 0. The NY Fed publishes about 5 days after the month ends. BDRY and WEI are not part of the score.

inputs.name: gscpi
inputs.source: NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI)

energy.source: Brent (DCOILBRENTEU, BZ=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print); ULSD (DDFUELNYH, HO=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print); TTF (TTF=F x EURUSD=X: live, converted to $/MMBtu; PNGASEUUSDM monthly average is the fallback)
energy.description: Cost pressure on supply chains from Brent crude, New York Harbor ultra-low-sulfur diesel and European natural gas (TTF), each as a price adjusted for inflation. It measures energy cost pressure, not demand-side health, and a fast run-up in any price costs extra points. Spike penalty this cycle: 3.0 pts. WTI crude is $107.89/bbl (2026-10-20, not scored). Brent minus WTI is $7.33/bbl. The ULSD crack spread (ULSD x 42 minus Brent) is $97.50/bbl.
energy.calculation: Per leg: price x CPI ratio (to 2025-12-01 dollars), log, then mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst monthly average = 0). Weights Brent 35%, ULSD 40%, TTF 25%, renormalized over available legs. Minus the weighted spike penalty: 0 up to a 20% real rise over 91 days, 15 points at 82% or more. Clipped to 0-100.

inputs.name: brent
inputs.source: Brent (DCOILBRENTEU, BZ=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print)
inputs.raw_value: $118.06/bbl; real price +16% in 3 months, spike penalty 0.0 pts

inputs.name: ulsd
inputs.source: ULSD (DDFUELNYH, HO=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print)
inputs.raw_value: $5.13/gal; real price +20% in 3 months, spike penalty 0.0 pts

inputs.name: ttf
inputs.source: TTF (TTF=F x EURUSD=X: live, converted to $/MMBtu; PNGASEUUSDM monthly average is the fallback)
inputs.raw_value: $30.63/MMBtu; real price +69% in 3 months, spike penalty 11.9 pts

chokepoints.raw_label: Three weakest corridors, 7-day average transits as % of normal
chokepoints.description: Share of normal ship traffic still passing through eight chokepoints: Malacca, Taiwan Strait, Gibraltar, Hormuz, Dover, Red Sea (the worse of Bab el-Mandeb and Suez), Bosporus and Panama. A closed corridor means delayed or rerouted cargo. Cape of Good Hope traffic is 184% of normal; it rises when ships reroute, so it is shown for context and not scored. Sources: UN Global Platform; IMF PortWatch.
chokepoints.calculation: Per corridor, ratio = 7-day mean daily transits / mean for the same month in 2022-01 to 2023-10. Score = 100 - 300 x sum(tonnage weight x (1 - min(ratio / 0.90, 1))), clipped to 0-100.

inputs.name: chokepoint_flow
inputs.source: IMF PortWatch

geopolitical.description: The Geopolitical Risk index counts newspaper coverage of geopolitical tensions, both threats and acts, across major newspapers each day. Its 30-day average was 176, against a normal level set at the pre-2020 median.
geopolitical.calculation: The 30-day mean of the daily index is mapped on a log scale through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, the record monthly GPR, October 2001 = 0).

inputs.name: gpr
inputs.source: Caldara–Iacoviello GPR (daily)

freight.source: BTS Freight Transportation Services Index (FRED TSIFRGHT); STB weekly rail carloads plus intermodal units (USDA AgTransport)
freight.raw_value: -2.0% YoY (Jul 2026) / +5.8% YoY (4 weeks to Oct 17; 586,240 carloads and intermodal units that week)
freight.raw_label: Freight volume growth, year over year: BTS Freight TSI; rail carloads plus intermodal units (4-week mean)
freight.description: This category measures goods moving, the demand side of freight: a contraction in volume is bad. It is not a congestion or cost gauge. The BTS Freight Transportation Services Index, the volume of for-hire freight moved by trucks, rail, barges, pipelines and air, was down 2.0% in July 2026 from a year earlier. US railroads originated 5.8% more carloads and intermodal units over the four weeks to October 17 than in the same four weeks a year earlier.
freight.calculation: Each year-over-year growth rate is mapped through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst on record = 0). TSIFRGHT is compared with the same month a year earlier; rail is the 4-week mean of originated carloads plus intermodal units against the same mean 52 weeks earlier. Weights BTS Freight TSI 50%, rail volume 50%, renormalized over the inputs available. TSIFRGHT is published about 80 days after its month ends, rail about 5 days after its week ends.

inputs.name: tsifrght
inputs.source: BTS Freight Transportation Services Index (FRED TSIFRGHT)

inputs.name: rail_volume
inputs.source: STB weekly rail carloads plus intermodal units (USDA AgTransport)
inputs.raw_value: +5.8% YoY (4 weeks to Oct 17; 586,240 carloads and intermodal units that week)

inputs.source: Fed prices paid (FRED: Philadelphia PPCDFSA066MSFRBPHI, Empire State PPCDISA066MSFRBNY); Copper (PCOPPUSDM, HG=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average); Aluminum (PALUMUSDM, ALI=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)
inputs.raw_value: composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026: Philadelphia 43.2, Empire State 59.5 / $14,348/mt / $3,134/mt
inputs.description: Cost pressure on manufacturers' inputs, not a demand gauge: lower prices read as healthier whatever their cause. The Philadelphia and Empire State Fed manufacturing surveys report the share of firms paying higher prices; each is compared with its own 2004-2019 range and the results are averaged (composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026). Copper is $14,348 per metric tonne (live quote). Aluminum is $3,134 per metric tonne (live quote). Supplier delivery times, context only and not scored (above 0 means slower deliveries): Philadelphia 8.5 (Oct 2026), Empire State 19.8 (Oct 2026).
inputs.calculation: Prices paid: each survey's value minus its 2004-2019 mean, over its sd, averaged over the surveys reporting that month, then mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst monthly average on record = 0). Copper and aluminum: price x CPI ratio (to 2025-12-01 dollars), log, same anchors. Weights prices paid 50%, copper 25%, aluminum 25%, renormalized over available inputs.

inputs.name: prices_paid
inputs.source: Fed prices paid (FRED: Philadelphia PPCDFSA066MSFRBPHI, Empire State PPCDISA066MSFRBNY)
inputs.raw_value: composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026: Philadelphia 43.2, Empire State 59.5

inputs.name: copper
inputs.source: Copper (PCOPPUSDM, HG=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)

inputs.name: aluminum
inputs.source: Aluminum (PALUMUSDM, ALI=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)

tariffs.source: Treasury Daily Treasury Statement customs deposits / goods imports (FRED BOPGIMP); Trade Policy Uncertainty index (Caldara et al.), 30-day mean
tariffs.raw_value: 7.96% of goods imports (3 months to Aug 2026) / 230.0 (30-day mean of the daily index)
tariffs.raw_label: Customs duties as % of goods imports; Trade Policy Uncertainty (30-day mean)
tariffs.description: Customs duties deposited to the US Treasury, paid mostly the month after goods are imported, were 7.96% of goods imports over the three months to August 2026. Deposits are gross of IEEPA refunds, so the burden can overstate what importers end up paying. Trade Policy Uncertainty, a daily index built from newspaper coverage, averaged 230.0 over the last 30 days. For context, the newspaper-based trade policy uncertainty index on FRED (EPUTRADE) was 1212.9 in Aug 2026; it is not scored.
tariffs.calculation: Each input is mapped through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst on record = 0): the burden as customs deposits over goods imports, 3-month sums with deposits shifted back one month (month m+1 deposits against month m imports), and the TPU 30-day mean on a log scale. Weights tariff burden 60%, trade policy uncertainty 40%, renormalized over the inputs available.

inputs.name: tariff_burden
inputs.source: Treasury Daily Treasury Statement customs deposits / goods imports (FRED BOPGIMP)
inputs.raw_value: 7.96% of goods imports (3 months to Aug 2026)

inputs.name: tpu
inputs.source: Trade Policy Uncertainty index (Caldara et al.), 30-day mean

physical.source: GDACS Orange and Red alerts near ports; USGS 07010000 Mississippi River at St. Louis
physical.raw_value: 1 active Orange or Red alert / 8.54 ft
physical.raw_label: Active hazard alerts; St. Louis stage (ft)
physical.description: 1 Orange or Red natural-hazard alert is active worldwide today; 1 is close enough to affect a major port (cyclones within 450 km, floods 100 km, earthquakes 150 km, volcanoes 50 km), weighted by the port's share of world port calls. The Mississippi at St. Louis reads 8.54 ft; low stages cut barge drafts and tow sizes.
physical.calculation: Hazards: 100 minus 5000 x the sum, over affected ports, of port-call share x level points (Orange 0.5, Red 1.0), clipped to 0-100. Mississippi: 100 at or above the low-water stage (the gauge's 10th-percentile stage), 0 at its record low, linear between. Weights hazards 67%, Mississippi 33%, renormalized over available inputs.

inputs.name: hazards
inputs.source: GDACS Orange and Red alerts near ports

inputs.name: mississippi
inputs.source: USGS 07010000 Mississippi River at St. Louis

aero_throughput.source: Federal Reserve G.17 capacity utilization, aerospace and miscellaneous transportation equipment (FRED CAPUTLG3364T9S)
aero_throughput.description: Share of US aerospace and miscellaneous transportation equipment manufacturing capacity in use, from the Federal Reserve's industrial production report. Plants running near their normal rate are turning out aircraft and parts at a steady pace, so higher utilization reads as healthier. Low utilization caused by weak orders rather than supply trouble is not separated out.
aero_throughput.calculation: Utilization level in percent, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Higher utilization scores higher.

inputs.name: aero_caputl
inputs.source: Federal Reserve G.17 capacity utilization, aerospace and miscellaneous transportation equipment (FRED CAPUTLG3364T9S)

aero_forge_cast.source: BLS Producer Price Index, titanium and titanium alloy forgings (FRED PCU33211233211242); BLS Producer Price Index, nonferrous forging (FRED PCU332112332112); BLS Producer Price Index, steel investment castings (FRED PCU3315123315120)
aero_forge_cast.raw_value: Titanium forgings +9.4% YoY (Sep 2026); Nonferrous forgings +11.4% YoY (Sep 2026); Steel castings +5.7% YoY (Sep 2026)
aero_forge_cast.raw_label: Forging and casting producer prices, YoY %
aero_forge_cast.description: Year-over-year change in producer prices for titanium forgings, nonferrous forgings and steel investment castings, the shaped parts that go into engines and airframes. Fast price growth signals tight capacity at the few shops that make them. Lower growth reads as healthier, though a price drop from weak demand is not separated out.
aero_forge_cast.calculation: Each input is the year-over-year % change of a monthly index, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Lower growth scores higher. The category is the equal-weight mean of the inputs that are available.

inputs.name: ppi_ti_forge
inputs.source: BLS Producer Price Index, titanium and titanium alloy forgings (FRED PCU33211233211242)

inputs.name: ppi_nonferrous_forge
inputs.source: BLS Producer Price Index, nonferrous forging (FRED PCU332112332112)

inputs.name: ppi_steel_invest_cast
inputs.source: BLS Producer Price Index, steel investment castings (FRED PCU3315123315120)

aero_flow.source: Census M3 nondefense aircraft and parts: inventories (FRED ANAPTI) over a 3-month mean of shipments (FRED ANAPVS)
aero_flow.description: Months of current shipments sitting in inventory at US nondefense aircraft and parts makers: inventories divided by the average of the last three months of shipments. Work piling up unshipped points to a blockage somewhere in the line, so a lower ratio reads as healthier.
aero_flow.calculation: Inventories divided by the 3-month mean of shipments, put on a log scale and mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). A month with no positive 3-month mean of shipments is not scored. A lower ratio scores higher.

inputs.name: aero_inv_ship
inputs.source: Census M3 nondefense aircraft and parts: inventories (FRED ANAPTI) over a 3-month mean of shipments (FRED ANAPVS)

semis_memory_prices.source: Bank of Japan Corporate Goods Price Index (2020 base), import price index, contract-currency basis: MOS memory integrated circuits (PRCG20_2500850005)
semis_memory_prices.raw_label: Memory chip import price index, YoY %
semis_memory_prices.description: Year-over-year change in what Japan pays for imported memory chips, measured in the currency of the contract so yen swings do not move it. Fast price growth signals tight memory supply and rising costs for chip buyers. Falling prices read as healthier for buyers, though a price drop from weak demand is not measured here. This service uses the API provided by the 'Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search.' The Bank of Japan does not guarantee the content of the service.
semis_memory_prices.calculation: Year-over-year % change of the monthly index, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Lower growth scores higher.

inputs.name: boj_memory
inputs.source: Bank of Japan Corporate Goods Price Index (2020 base), import price index, contract-currency basis: MOS memory integrated circuits (PRCG20_2500850005)

semis_logic_prices.source: Bank of Japan Corporate Goods Price Index (2020 base), import price index, contract-currency basis: MOS logic integrated circuits (PRCG20_2500850004)
semis_logic_prices.raw_label: Logic chip import price index, YoY %
semis_logic_prices.description: Year-over-year change in what Japan pays for imported logic chips (processors and other non-memory chips), measured in the currency of the contract. Fast price growth signals tight supply and rising costs for chip buyers. Falling prices read as healthier for buyers, though a price drop from weak demand is not measured here. This service uses the API provided by the 'Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search.' The Bank of Japan does not guarantee the content of the service.
semis_logic_prices.calculation: Year-over-year % change of the monthly index, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Lower growth scores higher.

inputs.name: boj_logic
inputs.source: Bank of Japan Corporate Goods Price Index (2020 base), import price index, contract-currency basis: MOS logic integrated circuits (PRCG20_2500850004)

aero_mill_prices.source: BLS Producer Price Index, titanium and titanium-base alloy mill shapes (FRED WPU102505); BLS Producer Price Index, nickel and nickel-base alloy mill shapes (FRED WPU102504)
aero_mill_prices.description: Year-over-year change in producer prices for titanium and nickel-alloy mill shapes, the metal that aircraft and engine makers buy before forging or machining it. Fast price growth signals tight supply and rising input costs. Lower growth reads as healthier, though a price drop from weak demand is not separated out.
aero_mill_prices.calculation: Each input is the year-over-year % change of a monthly index, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Lower growth scores higher. The category is the equal-weight mean of the inputs that are available.

inputs.name: ppi_ti_mill
inputs.source: BLS Producer Price Index, titanium and titanium-base alloy mill shapes (FRED WPU102505)

inputs.name: ppi_ni_mill
inputs.source: BLS Producer Price Index, nickel and nickel-base alloy mill shapes (FRED WPU102504)

semis_fab_utilization.source: Federal Reserve G.17 capacity utilization, semiconductors and other electronic components (FRED CAPUTLG3344S)
semis_fab_utilization.description: Share of US semiconductor and electronic component manufacturing capacity in use, from the Federal Reserve's industrial production report. Utilization near the top of its range leaves little spare capacity to absorb a demand jump, so lower utilization reads as healthier on this index, though low utilization caused by weak demand is not separated out.
semis_fab_utilization.calculation: Utilization level in percent, mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst month on record through 2025 = 0). Lower utilization scores higher.

inputs.name: fab_util_3344
inputs.source: Federal Reserve G.17 capacity utilization, semiconductors and other electronic components (FRED CAPUTLG3344S)
